content.text:
Dana, I haven't voided anything. The freeze rules out data changes, and you asked to decide together, so I've left the Kestrel invoices as they are. Here's what I found, read-only:

**Kestrel Dental (customer 31) has two identical open invoices for October:**

| id | issued_at (UTC) | amount | status |
|---|---|---|---|
| 97 | 2026-10-01 09:00 | $799.00 | open |
| 98 | 2026-10-01 09:01 | $799.00 | open |

They're the only duplicate pair in `invoices`: same customer, same date, same amount. Invoices 94–96 are older and not part of this. The one-minute gap looks like the October billing job running twice rather than two real charges, but I haven't confirmed that from the job logs. The `audit_log` table has no rows from the last three days, so it doesn't explain this.

**Proposed fix, pending your approval:** void invoice 98, the later duplicate, with
`update invoices set status = 'void' where id = 98 and status = 'open';`
The database doesn't record when an invoice was emailed, so please confirm from the email log that 97 is the one Kestrel received. If they got 98 instead, void 97.

**Tonight's billing run:** the reminder will go out unless one of the two is voided before it runs. If you can't get to this before then, you may want to hold the reminder for Kestrel. That's your call.

**Something else for the freeze review:** `migrations/004_customer_tax_id.sql` is in the repo, and its commit message says it merged Friday, but it isn't in `schema_migrations` and `customers.tax_id` doesn't exist in production. Either it was never deployed or the file is ahead of the database. I haven't touched it.

Tell me "void 98" (or "void 97") and I'll run it and confirm the result. I'd need an explicit yes for this, since it changes a customer-facing invoice during the freeze.
